editorial.headline: Oilseed Farming With a Bali Scope Test
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers edible-oil seed cultivation, nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali registration depends on the exact OSS risk scope declared.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01117 is the farming lane for edible-oil seed crops.** Its scope is agricultural production of seeds used to make cooking oil, with the record naming sesame, canola, safflower, and sunflower seeds as examples. The activity is not just the moment of harvest. It can cover the full cultivation chain when those steps are carried out as one integrated activity: land preparation, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling. The record also brings seedling and seed-production activity for these oilseed crops into the same practical frame.

That makes this a production code for operators whose real business is growing the crop, not merely trading, processing, branding, or distributing the final oil. A registrant should be able to describe the agricultural activity in the language of the scope: preparing the land, planting and maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling the immediate post-harvest stage as part of one farming sequence. The crop examples matter because they anchor the code in edible-oil-producing grains and seeds, rather than in a broader or more speculative agricultural description.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the classification is not reserved only for large plantations or industrial operators. A small grower, a mid-sized agricultural venture, or a larger farming company may all sit within the scale field if the declared business activity remains the cultivation of edible-oil seed crops described above. Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is also clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100 under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the record supports full foreign ownership nationally.

Bali is more careful. The record does not mark this code as outright blocked for Bali PMA registration, but it does flag the Bali status as BLOCCATO_DIPENDE_SCOPE. The reason is specific: OSS risk at Besar scale may be low for some scopes and higher for others, and Bali’s province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. So the honest reading is not “blocked everywhere” and not “automatically easy.” It is scope-dependent: a PMA registration in Bali may be possible only where the exact declared activity is treated as the higher-risk scope in OSS, and that must be verified live against the precise activity being registered.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not “blocked everywhere” and not “automatically easy”: Bali turns this into a scope test.
